chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Lennie Tristano's coldness
summary: Mingus says the coldness is real and tells a story about Tristano advising a bandmate about his new wife.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. Lenny was -- I never knew whether Lenny was as cold as he always seemed to me. There was a kind of a --
He's as cold as he seems to be.
Yeah, ice. Strange. Well, it comes out in his playing.
You said it comes out in his playing?
Yeah. I mean, his playing is always --

Woody Dennis told me, he just married his girl and Lenny was always telling the guy that any girl -- girls would want to ball everybody in the band. And so he say, started telling him, Lee, put your head down by her foot, (inaudible), put your arms around her here. He couldn't see the things he was telling to do, making all this -- so Woody said, you're crazy, man, this is my wife. He said, all women aren't like you think they are, and walked out. And they weren't friends for a long time.
